sections.title: Start here
sections.intro: Each of these serves three or more papers, so they are listed once here instead of under every subject.

items.name: UPSC previous papers
items.use: Question patterns, exact syllabus wording and timed practice. The only official source for CSAT, Essay and GS4 case studies.

items.name: NCERT textbooks
items.use: Basics in history, geography, polity, economy and science; Class 6–10 Maths for CSAT.

items.name: PIB Research Unit
items.owner: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of I&B
items.use: The government's own account of schemes, reports and visits; Year-End Reviews are good for revision.

items.name: Economic Survey
items.owner: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
items.use: The best yearly source of economy data and policy reasoning; its thematic chapters give essay material.

items.name: Union Budget
items.use: Budget at a Glance, Key to Budget Documents and the Budget Speech for budget concepts and new schemes.

items.name: NITI Aayog
items.use: Policy papers and indices for recommendations and "way forward" points.

items.name: Yojana, Kurukshetra and India Year Book
items.use: Free since April 2026 on Prasar Bharati’s WAVES app (the link is the official announcement). One theme in depth each month; the Year Book is the official fact reference.

items.name: Digital Sansad
items.owner: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats
items.use: Standing Committee reports, bills and ministers’ answers. Committee findings add weight to Mains answers.

items.name: India Code
items.use: The original text of Acts (RTI, Lokpal, RPA, DPDP) instead of summaries.

items.name: News On Air: Spotlight
items.use: Short audio analysis of current issues; Vishwa Darpan for international affairs.

notes.csat: Official CSAT material is limited to UPSC’s own Paper II archive and NCERT Class 6–10 Maths (both in Start here). For comprehension practice, PIB backgrounders and Economic Survey chapters are good official prose. No government source covers reasoning or decision-making.
notes.essay: No official source teaches essay writing. Use Yojana, Economic Survey thematic chapters, NITI papers and the India Year Book for content, and practise structure on UPSC’s own past essay topics.
notes.excluded: Left out because they are not official: PRS Legislative Research, Down To Earth / CSE, Wikipedia and all coaching portals.
